# Codebase Summary

This document provides a comprehensive summary of the codebase for the project.

## Overview
- **Project Name**: Codebase Project
- **Language**: Python
- **Framework**: Django
- **Database**: PostgreSQL

## Structure
The codebase is organized into several key components:

- **/app**: Contains the main application code
- **/tests**: Contains unit and integration tests
- **/migrations**: Contains database migrations
- **/static**: Contains static files such as CSS and JS
- **/templates**: Contains HTML templates

## Key Features
- **User Authentication**: Implements user login and registration.
- **API Endpoints**: Provides RESTful APIs for data access.
- **Admin Panel**: A built-in admin interface for managing data.

## Installation

title: Improve README description
body:
Hi!
Thank you for maintaining this repository.

I noticed that the README is very short, which makes sense for a simple example repository. However, as a beginner, I found it a little difficult to understand the exact purpose of this repository and how it is intended to be used.

Problem:
The README of this repository is intentionally very minimal. However, for beginners it is not immediately clear what the purpose of this repository is and how it is intended to be used.

As a new user, it can be confusing to understand why this repository exists and what someone should learn from it.

Proposed Improvement:
Add a short explanation at the beginning of the README (1–2 sentences) that explains:
- what this repository is for
- who it is intended for (e.g. beginners learning GitHub basics)

Why this is useful:
A short explanation would help new users understand the context of the repository more quickly and feel more confident when exploring GitHub for the first time.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The README contains a short explanation of the repository’s purpose
- The explanation is easy to understand for beginners
- No additional complexity is added

title: [Task] Establish Automated Issue Triage Protocol
body:
**Description:**
There is currently no strict triage process for incoming community issues, resulting in feature requests being mixed with critical bugs. We need to implement an automated labeling system and establish a triage protocol.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Create a GitHub Actions workflow for auto-labeling incoming issues (e.g., `bug`, `enhancement`, `security`, `documentation`).
- Draft and publish a triage protocol document detailing the weekly rotating "triage captain" responsibilities.

title: [Task] Expand E2E Testing for Multi-Cloud Environments
body:
**Description:**
The CI pipeline currently lacks end-to-end (E2E) testing for multi-cloud environments, which increases the risk of regressions when deploying new cloud provider integrations.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Allocate sprint time to build out a robust E2E testing matrix.
- Simulate evidence collection across AWS, Azure, and GCP simultaneously in the test environment.
- Integrate the multi-cloud E2E tests into the standard CI pipeline to block regressions.

title: [Documentation] Improve API Documentation Coverage for Reporting Module
body:
**Description:**
Several newly added REST endpoints for the reporting module lack comprehensive Swagger/OpenAPI documentation. 

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Add complete OpenAPI/Swagger annotations to all reporting module REST endpoints.
- Verify generated documentation is accurate and reflects actual request/response schemas.
- Ensure documentation is accessible via the standard `/docs` route.

title: [Bug/Enhancement] Handle Slack Integration Rate Limiting
body:
**Description:**
The alerting system occasionally hits Slack API rate limits during high-volume compliance drift events, causing missed alerts.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Implement exponential backoff and retry logic for the Slack API integration.
- Batch alerts where possible to reduce the total number of API calls during high-volume drift events.
- Add monitoring to log when rate limits are approached.

title: [Feature] UI for Custom Framework Mapping
body:
**Description:**
Users are requesting a UI feature to map custom internal policies to standard frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO, SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR). There is currently a gap in frontend development resources for this, but it is a highly requested feature for the reporting dashboards.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Create frontend UI components for custom policy mapping.
- Integrate the UI with existing backend mapping endpoints.
- Update user documentation to include instructions on how to use the custom framework mapping.

title: [Security] Fix PII Exposure in Audit Logs (Data Masking)
body:
**Description:**
PII (Personally Identifiable Information) is occasionally exposed in debug-level audit logs, requiring immediate patching for GDPR compliance. As a compliance tool, any mishandling of PII undermines the platform's core value proposition.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Audit logging mechanism must mask or redact all PII at the debug level.
- Introduce automated tests to verify PII masking in logs.
- Ensure compliance with GDPR data handling requirements.
- Backport fix to the upcoming v2.3.2 hotfix release.

title: [Enhancement] Update Terraform Provider for latest AWS resources
body:
**Description:**
The ComplianceHarbor Terraform provider needs to be updated to support the latest AWS resource types to ensure comprehensive infrastructure-as-code (IaC) scanning.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Map and implement support for new AWS resources in the Terraform provider.
- Pass all acceptance tests for the updated provider.
- Update the provider documentation with the newly supported resources.

title: [Bug] OPA (Open Policy Agent) Memory Leak during large Kubernetes manifest evaluation
body:
**Description:**
High memory consumption has been observed when evaluating large Kubernetes manifests in the policy engine. This memory leak is blocking enterprise users from scanning large-scale Kubernetes clusters.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Identify and resolve the memory leak in the OPA engine during large evaluations.
- Memory consumption should remain stable and within acceptable limits during large-scale K8s scans.
- Add profiling and benchmark tests for memory usage.
- Target fix for the v2.3.2 hotfix release.

title: [Tech Debt] Refactor Test Suite from unittest to pytest
body:
**Description:**
Migrate legacy unit tests from `unittest` to `pytest` for better maintainability and to leverage advanced testing features like fixtures and parameterization.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Convert all existing `unittest` test cases to `pytest`.
- Ensure the CI pipeline runs `pytest` successfully without any drops in test coverage.
- Remove `unittest` dependencies where applicable.

# Summary of the Codebase

This document provides an overview of the codebase, intended for new developers and contributors. The objective is to explain the structure, key components, and functionalities of the project.

## Key Components

- **Frontend**: The user interface is built using React.js, providing a responsive and dynamic experience.
- **Backend**: The server-side is developed with Node.js and Express, handling API requests and database interactions.
- **Database**: The project uses MongoDB for data storage and retrieval, ensuring scalability and performance.

## Directory Structure

```
/project-root
│
├── /src                # Source files
│   ├── /components     # React components
│   ├── /hooks          # Custom hooks
│   └── /utils          # Utility functions
│
├── /public            # Static assets
│   └── index.html      # Main HTML file
│
├── /server            # Server-side code
│   ├── /models         # Database models
│   ├── /routes         # API routes
│   └── server.js       # Entry point for the server
│
└── package.json       # Project metadata and dependencies
```

## Setup Instructions

1. Clone the repository:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World.git
   ```
2. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```
3. Start the development server:
   ```bash
   npm start
   ```

## Contribution Guidelines

- Fork the repository and create a new branch for your feature or bugfix.
- Submit a pull request with a clear description of your changes.
- Follow the coding standards and best practices outlined in the project documentation.

## Conclusion

This summary serves as a guide to understanding the structure and components of the codebase. For further information, please refer to the documentation or reach out to the maintainers.

This document provides an overview and summary of the codebase.

## Structure
- **src/**: Contains the source code for the project.
- **tests/**: Contains unit and integration tests.

3. **API Endpoints**: Implemented in `src/api.py`, these functions handle incoming requests.

- Python 3.x
- Flask for web framework
- SQLAlchemy for database interaction

## Installation
To install the dependencies, run:
```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Running the Application
To start the application, use:
```bash
python src/main.py
```

## Testing
To run the tests, execute:
```bash
pytest tests/
```
